Regenerative absorption cycle air conditioning using solar energy supplemented by a fuel cell /

The principal aim of this research was to design, fabricate and test an affordable air-conditioning system for low-income families living in hot countries. In order to achieve this aim, it was necessary to design the system that was simpe to construct, easy to maintain, energy efficient and environmentally friendly. The current study dealt only with the vapour absorption cycle air conditioning system because of its potential to use low-grade heat from various sources such as waste heat from power plants, solar radiation, geothermal, etc. The use of solar energy, as it is freely available, is obviously more attractive for the purpose. However, some means must be found to operate solar energy based air conditioning systems during hours of darkness, i.e. nights and overcase periods. Fuel cell was chosen as the auxiliary energy source. To enhance the heat transfer and thus the system performance, heat pipe was incorporated into the cycle. The total system including the heat pipe and a small fuel cell was designed, manufactured and tested and the results are presented.
